about: The 3D plant and litter species: chunky designed shapes built in code (growth/pieces.py), where each likes to grow (likes: 0..1 weights on base, damp, shade, wall_foot, edge, seam) and its gates. Sizes are tall (or across for flat things) in centimetres. Colours are sRGB hex, pulled 45 percent toward their own grey so they sit in the style. Gates are exact: a piece whose root is inside footfall 0.6, crown 0.7, keepclear 0.5, a puddle or within 5 cm of litter is never made. The "sites" block says where pieces gather and how many: a strip at the foot of walls, a strip along road edges, between ruts and where two ground surfaces meet (verge), a strip along fences and building lines, the joints between stones or boards, damp shady corners, and a thin background. Counts are at FULL growth (a derelict place); the look's growth amount scales them (plants by weeds_amount, litter by litter_amount, stones by half of it plus half). Stones (group "stone") lie only on unpaved ground (data/surfaces.json "unpaved"), are sized by a fact of the facts table (size_fact) and are seated part way into the ground (sink_share of their height).

sites.about: Where pieces gather and how many (growth/sites.py). width_metres is the strip's width (a strip narrower than one plan cell is widened to one cell). per_metre counts are per metre of a strip's length; per_100_square_metres counts are per 100 square metres of the area. centre_strip is the grass strip between the two wheel ruts of a road whose settings say "centre_grass": a close, low sward. All at FULL growth (see "about").
